newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky official admits stealing $4 million.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky official admits stealing $4 million.

text.p: A bureaucrat in Kentucky's state government pleaded guilty Monday to pocketing more than $4 million in tax refund checks issued to a company he created.
Prosecutors recommended a 14-year sentence for David Cheak, 42, for the scheme, which netted him $4.2 million, beginning in 1992.

Cheak, who worked in state government for 19 years, admitted that he used stolen computer passwords of fellow employees at the revenue department to write tax refunds for D & G Industries, a nonexistent company.

Authorities were able to recover roughly half the stolen money in cash and they confiscated farmland, machinery and livestock worth about $600,000. Cheak had also treated friends and family to meals, concerts and expensive shopping trips.

Although he said he was a manic depressive who was "driven" to steal, court-appointed psychologist Harwell Smith reported that Cheak "would like to believe, but does not demonstrate, that he had a mental illness that caused him to commit the alleged crimes."
